test.name: Probate: a testate file with a will, an executor's petition stating the death, and the court's proof
test.description: A will plus the court file it was proved in. Each part was produced by a different hand, so each takes its own row (genealogist ruling 2026-09-30): the will's statements are the testator's (self / primary); its execution and its witnesses are the witnesses' (witness / primary); the court's acts are the clerk's (official_duty / primary); and the executor's petition stating the death is family whose presence the file does not show (household_member / indeterminate). Record approved by the genealogist (2026-10-03).

Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania, Register of Wills, Will Book 14, p. 212

In the name of God, Amen. I, Thomas Flynn, of the Borough of Shenandoah, County of Schuylkill, being of sound mind, make this my last will and testament. I give to my beloved wife Mary Flynn my house and lot on Main Street for her natural life. I give to my son Patrick Flynn my mining tools and one hundred dollars. I give to my daughter Bridget Doyle fifty dollars. I appoint my son Patrick Flynn executor of this my will. Signed and sealed at Shenandoah this 4th day of March 1885. Thomas Flynn, his mark. Witnesses: Owen Brennan, James Gallagher.

Petition of Patrick Flynn, executor, filed 20 November 1888: that the said Thomas Flynn died at Shenandoah on 11 November 1888.

Proved 22 November 1888 before the Register of Wills of Schuylkill County, and letters testamentary granted to Patrick Flynn the same day.
</record-data>
